finding.summary: The `tableCellRange` skip test uses a collapsed range, so the collapsed early-return already satisfies it; the tableCellRange guard is untested
finding.evidence: The fixture's anchor and focus are both offset 8, so `expandRangeForLinks` returns `range` from the collapsed-range guard before it ever matters that `range.tableCellRange` is set. `expect(expandRangeForLinks(doc, cellRange)).toBe(cellRange)` therefore passes even if `if (range.tableCellRange) return range;` is deleted. No test passes a non-collapsed cell range (the shape a real cross-cell drag produces), so offset mangling in cell-range mode would ship green.

verdict.reason:
The finding's central factual claim is not present in the repository. It asserts the tableCellRange test fixture has "anchor and focus both offset 8" (collapsed), so the collapsed-range guard would satisfy the assertion. In fact packages/docs/test/view/link-run.test.ts:276-284 builds cellRange with anchor offset 2 and focus offset 8 — a non-collapsed range. The collapsed guard at link-run.ts:209-214 requires anchor.offset === focus.offset and therefore does not fire.

Tracing expandRangeForLinks with the tableCellRange guard (link-run.ts:208) hypothetically deleted: anchorComesFirst (link-run.ts:172-179) returns true for same-block 2 <= 8, so the line 217 undefined bail does not fire; the linked() fixture (test:155-163) is "plain LINK plain" with the link spanning 6..10, so interiorLinkRunAt(block, 8) returns a run, making endRun truthy and skipping the line 226 bail; execution reaches line 230-232, which returns a freshly constructed object with focus offset 10. The assertion expect(...).toBe(cellRange) is an identity check, so it fails on both identity (new object) and value (offset 10 vs 8). The sibling test at test:165-176 independently proves that this exact 2..8 range expands to 2..10 when the guard is absent, confirming the guard is the sole reason the test passes.

The secondary claim "No test passes a non-collapsed cell range" is likewise false: this test does exactly that, and linkRunCoveringRange's cell-range guard (link-run.ts:129) is separately covered by a non-collapsed cell range (offsets 0 and 4) at test:429-439. The test is a genuine, non-vacuous test of the tableCellRange guard, not fake coverage.

searchedFor: grep rawAnchor|expandRangeForLinks|setSnappedRange across repo (only src + the two test files)
finding.summary: No test covers the pointer-gesture wiring of link snapping (setSnappedRange / rawAnchor) - drag and shift+click behaviour is only unit-tested at the pure-function level
finding.evidence: `expandRangeForLinks` is thoroughly unit-tested in link-run.test.ts, but nothing exercises `TextEditor.setSnappedRange`, its two mousedown call sites, or `updateDragSelection`. The whole stated rationale for `rawAnchor` - that dragging back out of a link un-snaps instead of ratcheting, and that shift+click re-extends from the raw anchor - has no test. selection-raw-anchor.test.ts only asserts that `setRange` nulls a field the test itself assigned, which is coverage of a one-line assignment, not of the ratchet behaviour it documents. Pointer-driven tests are feasible here: packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts:190 dispatches real `mousedown` events at canvas coordinates. A wiring mistake (rawAnchor not set on the drag-start path, snapping applied where the anchor was deliberately rewritten) would ship with a green suite and change selection behaviour users see on every drag over a link.

verdict.reason: A dedicated pointer-gesture test exists: packages/docs/test/view/link-snap-pointer.test.ts. It builds a real editor via initialize() and dispatches real mousedown/mousemove/mouseup events at coordinates obtained from the editor's own getCursorScreenRect(), covering every item the finding calls untested. Specifically: drag ending mid-link expands to the link end (:198-204); the exact rawAnchor ratchet rationale — press mid-link at 12, move to 13 so the anchor snaps to 6, move back to 12 and assert the selection is null (a ratchet would still report the whole link), then move to 4 and assert {anchor: LINK_END, focus: 4} (:206-226); shift+click re-extending from the raw rather than the snapped anchor, including the backwards case (:228-242); backward drag (:244-250); a drag that merely abuts the link not swallowing it (:252-258); double-click word-select snapping (:260-267); and word-select establishing its own raw anchor for a following shift+click (:275-284). These exercise setSnappedRange (text-editor.ts:2381), the rawAnchor assignment (:2385) and updateDragSelection (:2221, reached from the mousemove handler at :2148). The test is not vacuous — assertions are exact-value toEqual on anchor/focus offsets that would fail under the wiring mistakes described — and not over-mocked: only canvas getContext('2d'), getBoundingClientRect geometry and requestAnimationFrame are stubbed, while the snapping/selection logic is real. It also ships two explicit control tests (:188-196, :269-273) whose stated purpose is to keep the snapped-range assertions honest if offsets stop resolving. packages/docs has no vitest.config, so vitest's default include glob picks the file up under the package's "test": "vitest --run" script (package.json:36). The finding's search account is also inaccurate: the grep it cites returns three test files, not two, the third being link-snap-pointer.test.ts.
